messages:
elaine: heads up — found a weird ESM/CJS resolution bug with our sampleapp when using an alias pointing to a local symlinked package (pnpm workspace). repro steps below, reproduces on Vite + also shows up in Rollup build for edge target.

elaine: steps to reproduce (short):
1) git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sampleapp.git && cd sampleapp
2) pnpm i && pnpm --filter sampleapp dev
3) add alias in vite.config: alias: { '@lib': path.resolve('../lib') } where ../lib is a local workspace package that builds both dist/index.mjs and dist/index.cjs.js

sam: which bundler/version? vite or rollup or webpack?

elaine: Vite 4.3 + esbuild deps, but also hits when we use rollup to produce an edge-compatible bundle.

owen: repro I used:
- pnpm link ../lib (symlink)
- vite dev -> open app -> import from '@lib' returns object with default === undefined
- build for edge (target: 'es2022') -> runtime error: "ReferenceError: require is not defined"

owen: minimal package.json in ../lib: 
{
content:
"name": "lib",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "main": "dist/index.cjs.js",
  "module": "dist/index.mjs",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}

owen: the problem seems to be that some bundlers/alias resolvers prefer the "main" field or resolve the symlink to the package root and then pick up the CJS entry (index.cjs.js). when the edge runtime executes it, "require" calls blow up.

sam: can you paste the runtime error?

owen: console error from edge node: 
Uncaught ReferenceError: require is not defined
    at dist/index.cjs.js:3:1
    at async Module.evaluate (edge-runtime.js:45)

tian: quick workaround — add explicit exports map in package.json with conditional exports to prefer the ESM entry for import: 

  "exports": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  }

this forces modern bundlers to pick the ESM path. also ensure "module" and "exports" align.

natalie: typings note: consumers doing "import type X from "@lib"" still worked but TS path resolution with alias sometimes picks up root tsconfig and not the dist types. add "types": "dist/index.d.ts" and add "exports.types" explicit to avoid mismatch.

elaine: temporary local fix was to change vite alias to point at dist/index.mjs directly instead of package root: alias: { '@lib': path.resolve('../lib/dist/index.mjs') } — that made the dev server and edge build happy. but obviously not ideal for workspaces.

sam: do we have a reproducible test we can add to devex e2e?

ci-bot: [ci] failing job: sampleapp-edge-e2e — import-resolution-alias-symlink (flaky) — see build 4721 logs.

elaine: ok can someone file a GH issue with steps + paste the minimal repo + note: pnpm symlink + vite alias + package.json missing conditional exports -> recommends adding exports.import and module field. tag with DX and bundler? @owen @tian :thinking:

owen: will open issue and include a tiny repro repo (public) and mark regression risk. will add a test case that switches the alias to the package root vs explicit mjs entry.

natalie: also add a note in SDK onboarding guide about prefer adding conditional exports for packages we expect to import in edge runtimes. saves a lot of confusion. :+1:

elaine: thanks — assigning to owen to follow up. summary: alias->symlink can resolve to CJS main; explicit exports/import entry or point alias to mjs fixes it; add CI e2e to catch.

sam: fyi — I ran across a related TS typing mismatch: when rollup resolves to cjs the generated d.ts import shapes differ. adding explicit "types" and exports.types fixed it for us.

elaine: closing the thread for now, please post issue link when created.
